http://www.advertiser.ie/galway/article/.text: The ancestral village of Menlough, East Galway, will once again become the focal point for the global Mannion diaspora when it hosts the Thirteenth Annual International Mannion Clan Gathering from Friday, 14 August to Sunday, 16 August 2026. Coinciding with the opening of National Heritage Week, the three-day celebration promises a rich programme of history, culture, genealogy and traditional Irish heritage. Festivities begin on Friday evening at 7.00 pm in Thompson’s Pub, Menlough, with registration and a welcoming reception, offering visitors from Ireland and overseas an opportunity to meet fellow clansfolk. The official opening will be performed by Galway County Heritage Officer Marie Mannion, who will extend a welcome on behalf of Galway County Council. The opening evening also features an illustrated presentation on the history and heritage of the Mannion Clan by clan historian Dr Joe Mannion, tracing the story of the Ó Mainnín family through the centuries. The programme concludes with a performance of traditional Irish sean-nós dancing by champion dancer Meadhbh Ní Chualáin. Saturday’s events centre on a guided tour of the Mannion Clan Historical Trail, led by Dr Joe Mannion. Participants will gather at Frank Mannion’s Lounge Bar in Abbeyknockmoy before travelling to a number of sites closely associated with the clan’s remarkable past. Among the locations visited will be Killaclogher, Clooncurreen and the site of Menlough Castle, together with the ancient ceremonial mound at Ramore in Mullaghmore West. It was here, in May 1584, that a landmark agreement between the two principal branches of the Mannion Clan was drafted under Brehon Law by a Mac Egan lawyer. The tour will also include Ballymannion, a sub-townland central to the historic Ó Mainnín legal deed. Abbey visit Following refreshments in Menlough, the group will visit Kilconnell Abbey, where John, son of Malachy, the last recorded Chief of the Name of the Mannion Clan, was buried in 1648 alongside two of his kinsmen from the clan’s traditional stronghold of Mionlach Uí Mhainnín. The final stop will be at the battlefield of Finnure, near Loughrea, where the reigning Ó Mainnín king of Soghan was killed in AD 1135 during a fierce conflict between the O’Connors of Connacht and the O’Kellys of Hy Many. Local historian Paul O’Donnell will provide an historical account of the battle. Saturday evening returns to Thompson’s Lounge Bar, where Jim Hollarn, the clan’s genetic genealogist from San Diego, California, will present the latest developments in the Mannion Surname DNA Project. This will be followed by a family history and genealogy session with Noel Murphy and Peadar Ó Mainín of the Rosmuc Area Genealogy and DNA Group. The gathering concludes on Sunday with a full programme in Menlough, including a Clan Mass celebrated by Fr Colm Mannion OP, a piper-led international clan parade and an engaging presentation on medieval and early modern Irish clothing and weaponry by Proinsias Mag Fhionnghaile, chieftain and historian of the McGinley Clan. The weekend will finish with the annual Mannion Clan barbecue overlooking the site of the former Ó Mainnín chieftains’ castle, followed by a traditional Irish music session featuring Fr Colm Mannion, Alan Mannion and friends. Contributions from gathering participants will add a fitting finale to the celebrations. Visitors are expected from across Ireland as well as from the United States, Canada, England and Latvia, reflecting the worldwide reach of the Mannion family. While the gathering celebrates the history of the Mannion Clan, attendance is open to everyone with an interest in Irish heritage, local history or genealogy. Further information is available by emailing [email protected] . The mission was supposed to last about 10 hours, but the SpaceX team decided to end it early. The ship deployed 26 "next generation" Starlink V3 satellites, joining the existing constellation which deliver broadband internet on Earth. SpaceX describes Starship as "the world's most powerful launch vehicle ever developed" and says it will eventually carry crew and cargo "to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond". https://english.news.cn/20260924/17d9b11.text: Slovakia to halve 2nd-class train fares amid rising fuel prices Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-24 00:14:15 Photo taken with a mobile phone on Sept. 21, 2026 shows a train arriving at Main Railway Station in Bratisalva, Slovakia. Slovakia will cut second-class passenger train fares by 50 percent for one month starting from Oct. 1, Prime Minister Robert Fico announced Wednesday after a government meeting. (Xinhua/Liu Haodong) BRATISLAVA, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- Slovakia will cut second-class passenger train fares by 50 percent for one month starting from Oct. 1, Prime Minister Robert Fico announced Wednesday after a government meeting. The measure, approved on the proposal of the Slovakian Transport Ministry, will initially remain in effect for 30 days. Subsequently, it will be reviewed on a monthly basis, Fico said. "Slovakia is currently facing a sharp rise in fuel prices with a direct impact on the economy and households, whose costs for private car transport are increasing. One of the possible solutions is to shift from private car transport to passenger rail transport," the ministry said in its explanatory report. The measure is primarily intended for people who use trains regularly to commute to work or school, or for other daily needs. The 50 percent reduction will apply to all second-class, single-journey tickets, as well as weekly and monthly season tickets. The temporary fare reduction is expected to reduce railway operators' revenues by about 4.3 million euros (4.9 million U.S. dollars) over the 30-day period, while increasing their costs by around 1 million euros (1.14 million dollars). The government is also considering measures for regional bus transport. Slovakian Transport Minister Jozef Raz has been tasked with preparing by Sept. 30 a proposal under which the state will reimburse self-governing regions for one third of their spending on suburban bus services if they reduce fares by 30 percent. ■
